chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: 'The one who wants that Allah should shade him on the Day when there is no shade except His shade' — saying it three times, and the people feared to ask him, so he said: 'Let him grant respite to the insolvent, or waive for him from his right.'

key_terms.لِيَدَعْ لَهُ مِنْ حَقِّهِ: Let him waive for him from his right
key_terms.مُعْسِراً: The insolvent (one who cannot pay immediately)
key_terms.يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ: The Day when there is no shade except His

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of granting respite to a debtor according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the eschatological reward of divine shade directly to the practical act of *tadil* (respite) or *takhfir* (forgiveness) of debts, emphasizing that financial mercy is a tangible manifestation of piety. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that interpersonal economic justice is not merely a legal obligation but a spiritual mechanism for securing Allah's protection on the Day of Resurrection, where no other shade will suffice.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who wants that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> should Shade him on the Day when there will be no shade except for His<sup>azwj</sup> Shade’ – saying it three times and the people did not have the courage to ask him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him respite the insolvent (give relaxation to that who owes you), or waive (something) for him from your rights’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once, spoke to us and repeated the following phrase three times. ‘If one wishes that Allah provide him shadow on the Day when there will be no shadow except His shadow,’ and no one had the courage to ask him to explain, he (Imam) then said, ‘He should extend the due date of repayment of a loan for a borrower who has difficulty to pay back, or partially waive it in his (debtor’s) favor.’”
